title: Design System: Energy Map Calorie Tracker

display.purpose: One per screen, always the screen's own name. The only place font-black is allowed.

headline.purpose: Card titles, fullscreen modal titles, the hero calorie figure.

title.purpose: Section titles inside a card and generated food names.

body.purpose: Row and paragraph copy; the support line drops to text-sm (0.875rem).

label.purpose: The muted line above a reading. 118 uses of text-[11px] - the app's most common size.

numeric.purpose: The emphasised reading in a card or tile; tabular figures wherever two numbers are compared.

shadows.name: shadow-xs
shadows.purpose: Stat chips, selected segmented options, small inset buttons.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Range thumbs and small raised controls.

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: The standard screen card and inner session row.

shadows.name: shadow-xl
shadows.purpose: A card that must read above another card.

shadows.name: shadow-2xl
shadows.purpose: Modal sheets and the glass tracker reading card.

shadows.name: card-sheen
shadows.purpose: Top-edge light on every rounded-2xl bg-surface card. Transparent on the light themes.

shadows.name: action-glow
shadows.purpose: Filled action buttons only, and only while enabled. Accent variants substitute their own hue.

motion.name: ease-emphasized
motion.purpose: The house curve: modal entrance, wheel pickers, settings page swaps, chart entrances, portion sheet.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: Carousel settle and the tab-bar icon colour crossfade - long tail, no overshoot.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: 150-200ms fades and the theme view-transition cross-fade.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Modal entrance and dropdowns; the modal backdrop itself fades over 180ms.

motion.name: duration-settle
motion.purpose: Carousel settle and its drag-linked chrome.

motion.name: duration-theme
motion.purpose: Root cross-fade on a theme change (View Transition API).

narrative.overview:
This is a device you read, not a page you browse. Every screen is a stack of inset panels — a background slate, a raised card, a recessed row inside it — and each panel exists to hold one reading or one action. Nothing is framed for atmosphere: the frame is the hairline, the reading is the number, and the colour is either the working blue that means "you can touch this" or one of fourteen encoder hues that names a quantity.

The atmosphere is quiet, technical and exact. Darkness is the working condition — the app is used on a phone at 6am for a weigh-in and at 10pm for a ledger review — so the neutral ladder is a cool slate and text is white or a muted slate, never pure black on pure white. Density is deliberate but never cramped: a card carries its own heading, one emphasised number, and a support line, and then stops. The one moment of looseness is the glass chrome (tab bar, tracker reading card), which stays glass because it sits over content it must not erase.

Motion is treated as instrumentation, not as delight: entrances are short (140–200ms) fade-and-rise moves; settles are compositor CSS transitions at 350ms on an exponential ease-out; state changes are a sub-1% scale press and a brightness step. Every animation has a `prefers-reduced-motion` opt-out, because an instrument that wobbles is an instrument you stop trusting.

The design's anti-reference is dashboard theatre: gradient hero cards, glow for glow's sake, a coloured border-left announcing importance, or a big number with nothing behind it. Where a neighbouring fitness app sells momentum, this one sells a number you can audit down to the formula that produced it — and the visual system has to look like it can be audited.
keyCharacteristics: One working accent — Signal Blue — carries interaction; the other thirteen accents encode values, categories and states, never decoration.
Three neutral slates (`chamber` → `panel` → `rail`) separated by 1px hairlines carry all structure; borders are never heavy.
Numbers are the content: a dedicated digit face (Barlow, digits-only subset), tabular numerals wherever two values are compared, and a 2xl/3xl bold figure beside an 11px muted label.
Cards on cards: 21 `rounded-2xl bg-surface` screen cards hold `bg-surface-highlight/50` rows, tiles and insets — nesting is the layout grammar, at two levels and no more.
Depth is tonal first, ambient second: a theme-tinted shadow scale plus a faint top-edge sheen (`--card-sheen`), never a shadow that appears on hover.
Glass is an effect with a job, used at full strength in exactly two places (floating tab bar, tracker reading card); lighter blur belongs to sticky chart headers and transient toasts.
Every number traces to an input; absence is shown as `—` or "No entries yet", never as a zero.

rules.name: The One Working Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue owns every interactive state. If a control needs to look tappable, it is blue, a tinted blue (`/10` fill, `/20` border), or neutral — never another hue. An accent that is not blue must be reporting a value.

rules.name: The Encoded Hue Rule
rules.body: A hue may appear only where it names a quantity, a category or a state. Red on a trash icon is a state; red on a heading is a decoration and does not ship.

rules.name: The Absence Rule
rules.body: Missing data is `—`, "No entries yet", or "Need more data" in Muted Slate. Never a plausible zero, never an interpolated claim, never a green tick for an untracked field.

rules.name: The Digits Are Data Rule
rules.body: Use `tabular-nums` on any figure that sits beside another figure, and never set a number in a different family by hand — the font stack already routes digits to Barlow. A proportionally-set column of numbers is a bug you can see.

rules.name: The One Black Title Rule
rules.body: Exactly one `font-black` per screen: the screen title. Card and section headings stop at `font-bold`; row lead lines stop at `font-semibold`. Emphasis comes from weight and size, never from a colour change alone.

rules.name: The Label Stays Muted Rule
rules.body: A label is Muted Slate and small; the value is Plate White and large. Grey out the label, never the reading.

rules.name: The Theme-Tinted Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth is mixed from `--overlay-base`, never from flat black. A hardcoded `rgba(0,0,0,…)` shadow is off-palette on three of the eight themes (Dawn's warm charcoal, Dusk's night plum, Midnight's ink) and flattens the rest.

rules.name: The Thumb Answers, Not the Shadow Rule
rules.body: State is carried by a sub-1% scale press (`0.985` generic, `0.98` primary, `0.99` cards) and a brightness step, plus a blue outline ring on `:focus-visible` (2px, 3px offset, 12px radius). Shadows are static: a shadow that grows on hover reads as a web page, not an instrument.

rules.name: The Glass Has A Job Rule
rules.body: `backdrop-blur-2xl` appears in exactly two places — the floating tab bar and the tracker reading card. Sticky chart headers and transient toasts use `backdrop-blur-sm`/`xs`, and the header gear is a translucent circle (`bg-surface/60`) with no blur at all. Glass marks "this floats over content and must let it through"; applied to a resting card it is decoration, and decoration is not in this palette.

rules.name: The Hairline First Rule
rules.body: Structure is stated by a hairline and a tonal step before it is stated by a shadow. If a region needs separating, move it one slate down before reaching for elevation.

rules.name: The Two Levels Rule
rules.body: Card inside card is the grammar; a third nested panel is a redesign signal. When a card needs more levels, split it into two cards.

dos: Do build from the semantic tokens (`bg-background`, `bg-surface`, `bg-surface-highlight`, `text-foreground`, `text-muted`, `border-border`) and the accent tokens. A new hue has to earn a meaning.
Do lead every card with one reading: a muted `text-[11px]` label, then a `text-2xl`/`text-3xl` bold value, then at most one muted support line.
Do put `md:` in front of every hover state, and pair it with `press-feedback` / `pressable-card` / `pressable-inline` plus `focus-ring`.
Do use `tabular-nums` whenever two numbers will be read against each other, and let the font stack route digits through BarlowDigits instead of setting a face by hand.
Do keep the floating bar's geometry in inline px and derive content clearance from `SCREEN_TABS_BOTTOM_CLEARANCE_PX` (102px) rather than hardcoding padding.
Do show absence honestly: `—`, "No entries yet", "Need more data", or a dedicated empty card with the action that fills it.
Do respect the safe-area variables and the keyboard inset (`max(...)`, never a sum) on anything pinned to the bottom, and give every animation a `prefers-reduced-motion` opt-out.
Do scale type with `--font-scale` and layout with `--density`; if you add a new `text-[Npx]` size, add it to the override block in `index.css`.
donts: Don't hardcode a colour — no `bg-slate-800`, `text-white`, `border-slate-700`, `text-blue-400`, and no `rgba(0,0,0,…)` shadow. Literal white/black at low alpha is permitted only for lighting (sheen, top-light, inset highlight), never for a hue.
Don't use a bare `hover:`; on touch it leaves a stuck state. `group-hover:` follows the same rule.
Don't add gradient text, decorative radial glows, coloured `border-left`/`border-right` accents, or a shadow that appears on hover.
Don't use `font-black` twice on one screen, or promote a card heading to display size — emphasis is one step, not two.
Don't put `backdrop-blur` on a resting card, or introduce another full-strength glass surface without a reason the user would notice.
Don't nest a third level of panels; split the card instead.

Don't hand-roll a wheel, a switch, a segmented control or a modal stack — the wheel picker, `BinarySwitch`, `SegmentedButton` and `ModalShell` are the primitives, and a second version of any of them is a drift bug.
Don't zero-fill missing data, invent an interpolation at a chart edge, or present a derived estimate as a measurement. `—` is the correct answer; it is also the one the product's honesty rests on.

Don't change the root font-size to scale text (it would grow the layout with it), write a modal's `height` for the keyboard, or position anything against the peek sliver — those are the platform contracts, not style choices.
